01

Why this system

Context

Barili is 42 barangays — and many conversations.

Official notices, safety information and residents' concerns move among residents, barangay offices, municipal departments and local organizations.

Each tile on the map is one barangay, drawn from its PSA 2020 boundary.

  • Residents
  • 42 barangay offices
  • Municipal departments
  • Local organizations

The design problem Draft · for academic review

When updates and follow-ups travel through separate channels…

  • residents may have difficulty finding relevant updates and tracking their concerns;
  • officials may have difficulty keeping a consistent record of communication.

Support with your actual requirements evidence — interviews, survey or approved manuscript.

The response

…E-sugid brings them into one shared system.

A resident Android app and a role-based web dashboard share one backend — so announcements, concerns and their updates live in one consistent record.

The drifting map is a visual metaphor, not research evidence.

02

What the study set out to do

General objective Draft wording

To design and develop E-sugid, a centralized community communication and information dissemination system — a Flutter-based Android application and a role-based web administration dashboard — to support official information access, targeted announcements, resident feedback, and coordinated communication among residents and authorized stakeholders in Barili.

Resident appFlutter · AndroidResidents
one shared record
Shared backendFirebaseAuth · Firestore · Storage · Functions · Messaging
scoped by role
Staff dashboardWebBarangay officials · Municipal departments · Organizations · LGU IT

Specific objectives Draft · align with manuscript

  3. Develop centralized dissemination — announcements and safety notices for intended audiences, with calendar and saved reading.Ch. 5–6
  4. Implement two-way communication — concerns to the right office with status updates; complaints kept separate.Ch. 4
  5. Implement verification and role-based administration with scoped access.Ch. 3 · 10
  6. Provide supporting information and guidance — services hub, local tools, assistant navigation.Ch. 7–9

03

A resident enters

Resident app · Home

Official updates come first.

  1. View My Barangay — the resident's own barangay page.
  2. Notices, Advisories, Events — filter the feed by type.
  3. Verified publishers — each post shows who issued it.
  4. Assistant — always one tap away.

Resident app · Services

Every community service in one hub.

  1. Emergency Center & Safety Alerts
  2. Bayanihan Works and Local Market
  3. Municipal Officials
  4. Town Map · Town Calendar · Barili Weather · Explore Barili

The centre + Concern button is on every main tab.

Staff dashboard · Resident Verification

Residents are verified before they take part.

Residents submit verification in the app; authorized barangay staff review it in the dashboard.

This capture shows an empty Pending queue. Proof-document review and approval are not shown.

Sign-in, registration with e-mail OTP and password recovery are in the app. The captured login screen is omitted because it shows a personal e-mail address.

04

A concern becomes a case

Resident app · Concern Center

Two doors: public concerns, private complaints.

“Report public problems like roads, water, or trash. Report private problems with a neighbor or person.”— Concern Center
  1. Start Filing Concern — this chapter's journey.
  2. File a Complaint — a separate, confidential workflow (step 6).

Step 1 of the concern form

The resident chooses who should handle it.

Goes to the barangay office — in our example, Barangay Vito.

Goes to the responsible municipal department of the LGU.

Goes to an approved organization that handles that kind of concern.

Next steps add details, photos and location; the form can be saved as a draft. Lines on the map illustrate the choice — they are not live data.

Resident app · My Activity & Barangay Board

The resident can follow it.

  • My Concerns lists the resident's cases as Active or Resolved, with status badges such as In Progress.
  • Unfinished drafts stay on the device until submitted.
  • The Barangay Board shows public reports in the barangay — so neighbors can see an issue is already reported.

Staff dashboard · Concerns

The receiving office sees it in its queue.

  1. Status tabs — Active · In Progress · Awaiting Information · Resolved.
  2. By category, with share of reports and a View action.
  3. Filter and Download for records.

Barangay staff see concerns sent to their own barangay. Counts are records from testing, not evaluation results.

Case lifecycle

Every change becomes part of the record.

Staff move the case forward. If they need more details, it waits for the resident; the resident's reply returns it to In Progress. Not every case passes through every stage.

Key actions appear in System Logs — for example Concern submitted and Concern resolved.

Still to capture: one matched case — submission → staff update → resident timeline → resolution.

Active In Progress Resolved
staff request details Awaiting Information resident replies

Resident app · File a Complaint

Private complaints stay separate.

“Only you and barangay officials can see this complaint. The other person will not see your report in the app.”— Complaint form

Staff handle complaints in their own queue, with stages such as To Review, Waiting for Reply, Hearings and Closed.

The staff complaint capture is withheld because it shows names in a dispute.

05

Information reaches the right people

Staff dashboard · Announcements

Every announcement has an intended audience.

Two published rows from the capture — select one to see its reach:

Staff publish notices, advisories and events now or on a schedule, for the audience their role allows.

Resident app · Updates & My Barangay

Residents find it where they look.

The same Sports Activity post appears in the community Updates feed and in Barangay Vito's verified feed. Residents can search, filter by type and bookmark.

These stills show the feeds; they do not by themselves establish notification delivery.

Resident app · Community Calendar

Events become dates.

The calendar shows scheduled community activities and what's coming up. In the source, event announcements are synced to the calendar by a Cloud Function.

Also in the source, not captured here: saving announcements to read later, including offline reading of saved items.

06

Safety and coordination

Resident app · Emergency Center

Safety information has its own place.

The Emergency Center shows active alerts and safety advisories — here in its normal all-clear state — with direct access to emergency hotlines.

No incident is shown in this capture.

Staff dashboard · Send Emergency Alert

Staff compose an alert in three steps.

Storm, Flood, Fire, Medical, Security, Road hazard, Utility or Other.

Title, details, safety action, and optional evacuation center and hotline.

Start and end time, and the audience: Registered residents of Barangay Vito will receive this alert. An emergency broadcast sends phone notifications with an alert sound.

Wizard captures only — final review, publication and delivery were not captured.

Resident app · Emergency Hotlines

Help is one tap away.

A hotline directory: the national 911 hotline and local agencies such as MDRRMO, BFP and PNP, each with call and detail actions.

A screenshot does not verify that each number is current. Also in the source, not captured: resident emergency reports and private organization-to-organization dispatch.

07

Neighbors and livelihoods

Resident app · Bayanihan Works

Neighbors ask for help — and offer it.

Help requests by category — Errands, Repairs, Farming and more — show how many helpers are needed and roughly how far away. Residents respond with I can help or post their own with Ask for Help.

Offers, acceptance, messaging and completion are in the source; this capture shows the request feed.

Resident app · Local Market

Local produce finds local buyers.

Listings show category, price per unit and availability. Buyers tap I'm interested; sellers use Sell an Item.

Coordination only — the app does not process payments.

Explore the municipality

Resident app · Barangay Map

The app knows Barili's barangays.

The map works with Barili's barangay boundaries — the same PSA-derived file this website uses to draw its 3D Barili.

Hover or tap a barangay on the 3D map to see its name and area.

Resident app · Explore Barili

Places to visit — and how to get there.

Destinations such as Mantayupan Falls in Campangga, with navigation modes Car, Moto and Walk and the remaining distance and time.

A still does not prove route accuracy or live tracking. The line on the 3D map is illustrative.

Resident app · Weather & Officials

Local context, close at hand.

Barili Weather shows current conditions and an hourly forecast (data source in the code: Open-Meteo). Municipal Officials lists the mayor, vice mayor and council members.

Captured weather is historical, and the app is not a weather-warning system. Confirm officeholders before discussing names.

Guidance through the assistant

Ask, and the assistant shows the way.

Answers can carry a button that opens the right screen. Try it here — the buttons move this presentation the way the app moves the resident.

Answer text is the app's own (English). The first answer is quoted from the source; the other two match the captured screen.

E-SUGID AssistantIntelligent Municipal & Barangay Guide
local quick answer

How it answers

Guidance — not decisions.

The three quick inquiries are answered on the phone, without a network call. Other questions go to a Cloud Function that calls Google's Gemini API with a server-side key, applies a rate limit, and only offers actions the user's role allows.

A verified cloud-generated answer has not been captured yet.

The assistant can

  • Answer the quick inquiries locally
  • Answer other questions through the cloud function
  • Offer a button to an existing screen
  • Reply in English or Bisaya for the quick inquiries

It does not

  • Submit concerns for the resident
  • Approve residents or staff
  • Decide complaints
  • Dispatch responders
10

The staff side

Staff dashboard · Barangay Captain, Vito

One console, scoped to the user's role.

Dashboard — barangay activity (concerns received and resolved), top concern categories, pending verifications.

Concerns — resident reports by status and category.

Announcements — published, scheduled, drafts and archive, each with its recipients.

Emergencies — active and resolved alerts; send an alert to the barangay.

Resident Verification — pending, verified, needs attention, rejected.

Barangay Team — officials and requests for new official accounts, which LGU IT approves.

Use the sidebar or press → to tour. Complaints are omitted (personal details).

11

How it is built

Architecture

Two clients, one Firebase backend.

  1. The app calls submitConcern.
  2. The function validates and writes the case to Firestore.
  3. The dashboard lists it for the receiving office.
  4. Staff updates are written back; the resident sees the status.
  1. Staff publish from the dashboard (now or scheduled).
  2. Firestore stores it with its audience.
  3. A trigger delivers notifications through Cloud Messaging.
  4. Event posts sync to the calendar.
  1. Staff call publishEmergencyAlert.
  2. The alert is stored for its barangay audience.
  3. A trigger sends the broadcast via Cloud Messaging.
  4. Residents can acknowledge in the app.
  1. Quick inquiries are answered on the phone.
  2. Other questions call askESugidAssistant.
  3. The function retrieves grounding records and calls Gemini.
  4. Only role-allowed navigation actions are returned.

Access and integrity

Rules are enforced on the server.

  • Staff accounts are created by trusted Cloud Functions; the public client can create resident profiles only.
  • Firestore and Storage security rules enforce role and entity boundaries, independent of the interface.
  • API keys for Gemini and e-mail stay as server-side secrets.

Describes implemented controls; this is not an independent security certification.

13

Conclusion

Contribution

One shared system for Barili's information — and its conversations.

Official announcements with intended audiences, concerns routed to the office that handles them, and staff work scoped by role — in one Android app and one web dashboard over one record.

Implementation shown

  • Resident app and staff dashboard (Obj. 2)
  • Targeted announcements and alerts (Obj. 3)
  • Concerns with status; separate complaints (Obj. 4)
  • Verification and role scoping (Obj. 5)
  • Services hub, local tools, assistant (Obj. 6)

Evidence pending

  • Requirements evidence (Obj. 1)
  • Evaluation results (Obj. 7)
  • One matched end-to-end case capture
  • A verified cloud assistant answer

Current limits

  • Offline use is limited to saved announcements
  • Maps, weather and cloud answers need connectivity
  • No payments; no guaranteed emergency response
  • Future work — to be added by the team
